steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch pan.

To make the cake: Mix flour, cinnamon, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the center and add sugar, oil, eggs, and vanilla. Mix with a wooden spoon until smooth. Stir in carrots, coconut, walnuts, and pineapple. Pour batter into the prepared pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 45 minutes. Allow cake to cool completely before frosting. (The center of cake may sink slightly as it cools.)

To make the frosting: Beat cream cheese and butter in a mixing bowl until smooth. Add confectioners' sugar; beat until smooth and creamy. Spread frosting on top of cooled cake. Slice into squares and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Carrot Pineapple Cake
raw_recipe.description: This carrot cake recipe with pineapple, walnuts, and coconut is made in one bowl, bakes up deliciously moist, and is topped with cream cheese frosting.

review.reviewBody: Understand that my baking skills are extremely limited. On the other hand, after having a piece of this carrot cake, nobody can tell! I did read these reviews closely, at least until the general techniques that make this good recipe even better began to become apparent. I added 1/2 teaspoon each of nutmeg and allspice to the dry ingredients, substituted 1/2 cup of apple sauce for 1/2 cup of the oil, and added 1 cup of golden raisins to the batter. I also doubled the frosting, and had plenty to frost the cake plus a little left over. Then, since I'm baking at an altitude of 8,000-feet, I increased the flour to 2-1/4 cups, decreased the baking powder to 1-1/2 teaspoons, decreased the sugar to 1-1/2 cups, increased the baking temperature to 375F and decreased the cooking time to 40 minutes. I made 2-9" rounds (parchment/grease/floured, of course) and they came out perfectly. Guess I better start a cake section in my home recipe book, because this one will be made a few times a year! Thanks, Linda! And thanks to all those real bakers who take the time and effort to make such great suggestions for us neophytes!

This cake is awesome! I reduced the sugar by 1/4 cup. Made them into cupcakes. Oven was reduced to 325 for 25 minutes. Perfect! Husband didn't even wait for the cream frosting. Said they were wonderful! Thanks for sharing your recipe. This is going to be my "go to" recipe.

Really good. The recipe didn't specify sweetened or unsweetened coconut. I used unsweetened and it worked. 
Would have like it a little moister. I'd maybe add a little more oil next time. Baked mine in two small loaf pans to be able to freeze one for later.

Delicious! I added little more cinnamon and some ginger and raisins. Omitted the coconut. Used half white and half brown sugar. Since the batter seemed heavy, I made it in three layers instead of two. For the icing I used 16 oz of cream cheese and maybe a cup of conf. Sugar and some vanilla.

Super moist. Instead of coconut I did 3 cups of carrots. Did cupcakes for 18 minutes. Also did Bundt cake for 45 minutes added some nutmeg. Nice and moist. Also did with coconut another time and it was still perfect

Excellent carrot cake. I made it with a mixture of gluten free flowers and baked it in a Bundt pan. After 50 minutes at 350, I reduced the temperature to 320 for another 15 minutes to fully cook. This may be because of the G F flower. Not sure. Excellent! No leftovers.

Changed the recipe quite a bit but still turned out great. I used whole wheat flour instead of all purpose. Added about 1 cup rolled oats. Used 1 cup grated zuchinni and 1 cup carrot. Also added chocolate chips and dried cranberries in addition to the walnuts and raisins. Omitted the pineapple and coconut (did not have on hand). Added about 1/4 cup OJ. Made frosting as directed. Everyone ate their whole portion to the last bite (including 3 year old twins).

Served as a Birthday Cake for 10 adults. Rave Reviews!

Changes that I made to suit my taste — 
CAKE
Used whole wheat pastry flour only, 1/4 c butter, 1/4 c applesauce, 1/2 cup avocado oil, 1 cup white sugar, 2 TBL honey, 2 1/2 c shredded carrot, undrained crushed pineapple.
FROSTING
12 ounces Neufchatel cheese
1/ c butter
3 c sifted powdered sugar
Wonderful flavor and a keeper! I am a diabetic and substituted 100G of EQUAL and a half cup cup of regular brown sugar and half cup of sugar free brown sugar.

Cannot rave enough about this recipe. Made 8 in rounds, baked 40min, did not drain the pineapple, substituted 1/2 Cup applesauce for 1/2 Cup oil, DELICIOUS!
Make extra frosting!!!

It was fantastic! Best ever Carrot Cake.
I made a few changes to try for a little more healthiness :-)
Used 1/2 C White sugar and 1/2 C organic brown coconut sugar.
Added 1/2 C unsweetened apple sauce
Used chopped pecans(walnut allergy)
In my oven it took less than the 45 minutes.
For the frosting we used a recipe that had a little less sugar, and added vanilla, and it was amazing- not too sweet.

I tweaked the recipe a bit, to suit what I had on hand. Instead of only cinnamon, I also added allspice, cloves, nutmeg & ginger. Instead of coconut, I added craisins. We skipped the nuts. This cake came out moist, and more like a spice cake, carrot cake hybrid. Delicious with the cream cheese icing!
Yummy carrot cake.
Good recipe very moist lots coconut for flavor. Will make again.
Delicious, add golden raisins and used pecans instead of walnuts
Great. No changes. Made 1/2 recipe for two of us.
Delicious Easy to follow Worth the Effort 👌
During Xmas I make more like a fruit cake with raisins or other dried fruit chopped maraschino cherries use mini bundt cake tin for baking, glaze with thinner icing or powder sugar.

This was delicious and my family loved it! They said it was the best carrot cake they’ve ever had! I only added half the carrots and half the coconut but the rest I kept the same. I will definitely be making this again!
Everybody at Easter dinner said it was the best Carrot Cake they have ever had!
